project.name: pr-review-pipeline
project.objective: GitHub-triggered multi-agent PR review system: four specialist lens agents (security, quality, test_coverage, docs) run in parallel on each PR, findings are verified for confidence, high-confidence findings auto-post as inline comments, mid-confidence findings go through human-in-the-loop approval, low-confidence findings are discarded but logged. LLM: local Ollama (qwen3:8b) via a thin provider port. Storage: Tiger Cloud Postgres. Queue: Redis+ARQ. Orchestration: LangGraph. VCS: GitHub App.

plan_approval.reason: Approved 9-task Phase 1 plan; Tiger Cloud provisioning still pending, will land before TASK-storage.

approval.reason: Reviewed spec content, scope, decisions and risks in conversation; approved as-is.

assumptions.text: Single 8B local model (qwen3:8b) is used for both a lens agent and the verify step; the confidence gate is therefore not an independent check. Confidence thresholds will likely need retuning and the HITL band may need to be wider than a stronger-model deployment would need.

claim_finding (FR-8) inserts the posted_findings row before the caller actually posts the GitHub comment. If the post node crashes between a successful claim and the actual VCS post, the finding is permanently unclaimable on retry (row already exists) and silently never gets posted -- no error, no re-post, no log. This is a known gap in TASK-storage's schema, not fixed here; the post node (TASK-hitl or wherever FR-8's caller lives) should either confirm-after-post (e.g. a posted_at update / two-phase claim) or this assumption should be revisited before the post pipeline is wired up.

decisions.title: LLM provider: local Ollama, not Anthropic
decisions.text: No Anthropic API key available; using locally-hosted Ollama (qwen3:8b) for all five AGENT_MODEL_* roles via a thin provider port mirroring VCSProvider, so a hosted provider can be swapped in later.

decisions.title: Phase 1 deploy target: local dev machine behind a tunnel
decisions.text: No hosting account for Phase 1. Webhook receiver runs on the local dev machine with an ngrok/cloudflared tunnel for a public HTTPS endpoint. Revisit hosting before treating this as always-on infrastructure.

decisions.title: Test repo for Phase 1 verification
decisions.text: github.com/varunbalwani/In-memory-Pub-sub-in-Go is the concrete repo used for the verification checklist's real test PR. The system remains general-purpose (installable on any repo), not hardcoded to this one.

decisions.title: Not a Niyo-org repo; no Jira-key commit convention applied
decisions.text: This is a personal project under projects/personal, not Niyo engineering work. Commits will not carry a Jira key by default per org convention, since that convention targets Niyo repos.

decisions.title: resolve_comment uses GraphQL resolveReviewThread
decisions.text: GitHub's REST API has no endpoint to resolve a PR review conversation thread; only the GraphQL mutation resolveReviewThread(input:{threadId}) does this. VCSProvider.resolve_comment therefore treats comment_id as a GraphQL thread node ID (e.g. PRRT_...), not a REST numeric comment id, and issues a POST to /graphql through the same authenticated installation-token client used for REST calls.

decisions.title: Lens agent output contract: model returns snippet, not fingerprint
decisions.text: Each lens prompts the model for a JSON array of {path, line, side, snippet, severity, confidence, rationale, suggested_patch}. Finding.fingerprint is computed in code as sha256(path|normalized_snippet|category), never trusted from the model, so it stays stable across line-number drift on resume (contracts.py docstring: 'not line number'). Docs lens gating (FR-3) is a path/symbol heuristic: README/docs paths, filenames containing 'cli', config extensions (yaml/toml/ini/cfg), or an added top-level def/class without a leading underscore in the patch body. FR-2's 'run in parallel' is satisfied by run_all_lenses() using asyncio.gather; LangGraph node wiring for the four lenses is a separate later task.

decisions.title: TASK-orchestration satisfies NFR-4 partially; durability deferred to TASK-storage
decisions.text: NFR-4 has two halves: (1) interrupt() must not block ARQ worker concurrency while a finding is paused, and (2) the checkpoint must persist so a paused job can resume later, potentially in a different worker process. This task proves (1): the graph pauses via interrupt(), returns control to the caller, and resumes from an approvals dict without re-running analyze/verify (test_graph_pauses_on_mid_confidence_and_resumes_without_reanalyzing asserts verify_calls stays at 1 across the pause/resume boundary). It does NOT prove (2): tests use langgraph's in-memory MemorySaver in a single process, which does not survive a process restart or a different worker picking up the resume. build_graph(llm, checkpointer) accepts any BaseCheckpointSaver so TASK-storage's Postgres-backed saver can be substituted without touching this module, but durability itself is unverified until that swap happens. Also deferred to TASK-storage/TASK-hitl: actually calling VCSProvider.post_review for the to_post bucket, the FR-8 idempotency check, and logging discarded (sub-floor) findings per FR-5/FR-9 -- this graph's output is the routed finding buckets (to_post/discarded), not a fully wired posting pipeline.

decisions.title: Confidence routing thresholds: AUTO_POST_THRESHOLD=0.85, DISCARD_FLOOR=0.3
decisions.text: SPEC.md's Risks section says thresholds are tunable and the HITL band should likely be wide, given a single 8B model scores its own findings (ASSUMPTION-8bf6c420), but gives no numeric defaults. Chose 0.85 auto-post / 0.3 discard-floor as a starting point matching that guidance (wide HITL band), read from AUTO_POST_THRESHOLD/DISCARD_FLOOR env vars per the NFR-3 config-key convention, not hardcoded. Expect retuning once real qwen3:8b confidence output is observed against real PRs (TASK-e2e-verification).

decisions.title: NFR-4 checkpointer durability is out of TASK-storage's scope as contracted
decisions.text: DECISION-2b35d850 assigned NFR-4's durability half (a Postgres-backed BaseCheckpointSaver so a paused LangGraph run survives a process restart / different worker) to TASK-storage. TASK-storage's actual contract (genesis brief) only lists FR-8/FR-9/FR-10 -- the findings/audit/outcome schema and idempotent pre-write check -- with no scenario or gate covering a checkpointer. Building langgraph-checkpoint-postgres wiring was not done here to keep this task's diff to its declared contract. NFR-4 durability remains unimplemented and should be its own bounded task (e.g. TASK-checkpointer) before it's relied on in production.

decisions.title: Finding gains a snippet field so TASK-hitl can re-anchor by content (FR-7)
decisions.text: fingerprint (contracts.py) is sha256(path|normalized_snippet|category), a one-way hash; agents.py computed it from the model's raw snippet but never retained the snippet itself, so nothing downstream had text to search the current diff for on resume. FR-7 ('re-anchor by fingerprint against the current diff') is impossible without that text. Finding gains an optional snippet: str | None field (default None keeps existing Finding(...) call sites and tests valid); agents.py populates it with the same normalized snippet used to compute the fingerprint. orchestration.py needed no change -- its interrupt() payload already uses finding.model_dump(mode='json'), which picks up the new field automatically.

decisions.title: TASK-hitl's /hitl/approve returns a routed, re-anchored decision -- it does not post to GitHub
decisions.text: create_app's /hitl/approve endpoint (pr_review/hitl.py) authenticates the approver via GitHub OAuth token (FR-6/NFR-5), checks repo ownership (fails closed on any non-200 from the collaborator-permission endpoint, since GitHub returns 403 -- not 404 -- when the caller's own token lacks access to ask), resumes the paused LangGraph run, and re-anchors each to_post finding's line against a freshly-fetched diff (FR-7, resolving the actual new line via hunk-header-aware patch walking, not just checking the snippet exists somewhere in the patch blob). It deliberately does not call VCSProvider.post_review or storage.claim_finding (FR-8) -- that belongs to a not-yet-created posting step, same shape as DECISION-4fed71f4's checkpointer gap. ASSUMPTION-cdc6fa50 (claim-before-post crash can silently drop a finding) applies directly to whoever builds that step. Also noted: check_repo_ownership calls the collaborator-permission endpoint with the approver's own token, so the check is bounded by what that token itself is allowed to introspect -- an App-installation-token-based check would be independent of the caller's own scope, and is worth revisiting if approvers ever have narrowly-scoped tokens. Also noted: resuming a (repo, pr_number) with no paused checkpoint currently raises inside graph.ainvoke rather than returning a clean 404/409 -- not fixed here, flagged for whoever builds the posting/resume-routing layer.

decisions.title: TASK-e2e-verification wiring: single-process app+worker, ASSUMPTION-cdc6fa50 is now live code
decisions.text: pr_review/app.py assembles the whole Phase 1 system as one process: FastAPI (webhook.create_app + hitl.create_app merged via merge_apps) plus an ARQ Worker run in-process as a background asyncio task (not arq's separate CLI), because the HITL endpoint and the worker's review_pr must share the exact same MemorySaver object (worker._MEMORY_CHECKPOINTER) for a resume to see a pause -- that only holds within one process, and DECISION-4fed71f4's Postgres checkpointer doesn't exist yet. This means a HITL pause does not survive a process restart; AC-2 is only verifiable within one continuous run of . pr_review/worker.py's post_findings function is the posting step DECISION-b3356b1f deferred: it now actually calls claim_finding (FR-8) then VCSProvider.post_review, so ASSUMPTION-cdc6fa50 (a crash between claim and post silently drops the finding) is reachable in running code, not just a documented future concern. LLMProvider gained complete_with_usage (pr_review/llm.py) returning (content, usage) rather than mutating shared state, specifically so concurrent lens/verify calls (asyncio.gather) can't cross-attribute token counts -- worker.AuditingLLMProvider acquires its own pooled connection per call for the same reason (a single shared asyncpg connection cannot serve concurrent queries; this was caught by a genuinely concurrent test, not reasoned about statically). scripts/verify_e2e.py is the task's gate: it checks observable evidence (GitHub review comments exist, no missing posted_findings vs audit rows, audit_log populated with no raw-content column) against a PR the human has already driven through the running system -- it does not orchestrate opening PRs, pushing commits, or approving HITL findings itself.

decisions.title: app.py env reads moved into lifespan; verify_e2e's AC-3 check now cross-checks claims against real GitHub comments
decisions.text: Follow-up to DECISION-7fc10dea after a second advisor pass: pr_review/app.py originally read GITHUB_APP_ID/GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH/GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET and opened the private key file at module import time, so import pr_review.app (any tooling, not just uvicorn) failed with KeyError unless the environment was already fully configured. All env/file reads now happen inside _lifespan, run only when uvicorn actually starts serving; app = FastAPI(lifespan=_lifespan) is importable with zero environment configured, verified via env -i. Shutdown now awaits worker.close() before cancelling worker_task (previously cancelled first, racing the worker's own cleanup). Separately, scripts/verify_e2e.py's AC-3 check originally just asserted posted_findings rows existed without comparing them to actual GitHub comments -- its docstring claimed to catch ASSUMPTION-cdc6fa50's crash-drop gap but the code never did. _check_claims_match_posted_comments now compares len(claimed) to the real comment count fetched via list_review_comments and fails on mismatch.

Ollama-backed LLM provider port with config-key model resolution (AGENT_MODEL_SECURITY/_QUALITY/_TEST_COVERAGE/_DOCS/_VERIFY), swappable for a hosted provider later
GitHub webhook receiver: HMAC verification over the raw body, event filtering, enqueues an ARQ job keyed by repo/pr/head_sha
GitHub App auth (JWT + installation token mint/cache) implementing VCSProvider: fetch_diff, fetch_file, post_review, resolve_comment
Four lens agents (security, quality, test_coverage, docs) mapping diff -> list[Finding]; docs lens gated to public-surface changes only
LangGraph graph: fan-out to four agents -> verify (confidence score) -> route (auto-post/HITL/discard) -> interrupt()/resume without blocking the ARQ worker
Postgres schema: findings table (idempotency key), audit table (model/tokens/latency, no raw content), outcome table; idempotent pre-write check
HITL approval endpoint (authn/authz/ownership check); on approval, re-anchor finding by fingerprint against current diff, fall back to file-level summary note if the line is gone
Behavioral verification against a real PR on the test repo: correct inline comments, HITL re-anchor after a push, idempotent retry, gated docs lens, audit content, cross-repo install
